summary: Floyd County, VA summit tower removed before 1987, believed 1986, as the area became a natural area preserve; the preserve is open to the public; no remains described.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia gives an approximately one-mile trail to the summit; WVTF (January 2026) gives a 2-mile trail. Both are kept and the story reports both.

The register lists the Virginia Department of Forestry as administrator of the tower site; the Department of Conservation and Recreation publishes the preserve's public access rules. Both are recorded.

notes_for_editor: No source gives a build date, builder, design, height or staffing for the Buffalo Mountain tower. Elevation: the register gives 3,971 ft (1,210 m) for the tower site; Wikipedia gives 3,960 ft (1,210 m) for the peak; the story gives neither. The DCR page carries 2020-era COVID closure text and 2026-27 hunting closures; only the access facilities and marked-trail rule were used. Brief said access unknown; now public (preserve) with no tower to climb.
